intro: To turn on keyboard shortcuts in Gmail on a Mac, open Gmail in your browser, click the gear icon, and choose See all settings. On the Settings tab, select Keyboard shortcuts on under the Keyboard shortcuts section, click Save Changes, and press ? to confirm.
tldr: The setting lives inside Gmail, in your browser. Apple's Keyboard settings do not switch it on.
The path is gear icon, then See all settings, then the Settings tab, then the Keyboard shortcuts section.
Select Keyboard shortcuts on, click Save Changes, then press ? (Shift + /) to confirm the shortcut list opens.
Use Command (⌘) on a Mac wherever Google's tables say Ctrl.
If keys still do nothing, check focus, browser extensions, cookies, and macOS shortcut conflicts.

blocks.text: Gmail's keyboard shortcuts sit behind a setting you have to choose. The switch lives inside Gmail, not in macOS, so you turn it on in your browser. Once it is on, you can move through your inbox and send mail without reaching for the mouse. This guide covers the browser steps, the Mac keys, and the fixes for when nothing happens.
Why the switch is in Gmail, not in macOS

Apple's Keyboard settings control shortcuts for macOS itself. Gmail's shortcuts belong to the Gmail page in your browser. Changing Apple's settings will not turn Gmail's shortcuts on. Google's help page is written for computers in general, and its steps apply on a Mac. Gmail also needs you to be signed in. Loading mail.google.com while signed out sends you to Google's sign-in page, so the settings stay out of reach until you log in.
Which browsers support Gmail keyboard shortcuts on Mac

Gmail runs in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge on a Mac. A third-party troubleshooting guide says Gmail works in those four browsers when cookies and JavaScript are on. If keys still do nothing, check that both are turned on before you change anything else. The browser is the only place this setting exists, so a browser problem can look like a shortcut problem.
The quick check: press ? to confirm shortcuts are on

The question mark is the fastest test. Make sure Gmail is the active window, and that your cursor is not in a text box. Press ? (Shift + /). If the Keyboard shortcuts dialog opens, the feature is on. If nothing opens, go back to Settings and check the section again before you try the fixes below.
Watch for one trap. Press ? inside a compose window and you type a question mark into your message. Click the inbox list first, then press the key.
Mac keys: use Command where Google writes Ctrl
Google's tables list Ctrl for PCs. On a Mac, press Command (⌘) in the same spot. Send is ⌘ + Enter. Bold is ⌘ + B. One shortcut exists only on Mac. Press ⌘ + ; to jump to the next misspelled word.

blocks.caption: Gmail shortcuts from Google's help page, by system

blocks.text: Which shortcut groups need the setting turned on

Google's page says several shortcut groups stop working until you turn shortcuts on. These are the actions, jumping, thread selection, navigation, and application groups. If one of those does nothing, the setting is the first place to look.

The compose and formatting groups carry no such note. If ⌘ + B does nothing after you turn shortcuts on, try the fixes later in this guide. Google also warns that shortcuts are not supported by every language or keyboard.
A worked example: bold a line and send without the mouse

Here is a short run through a real draft. Open Gmail, click Compose, and type a sentence in the message box. Select one word with a double-click or a drag. Press ⌘ + B, and the selection turns bold. When the draft reads right, press ⌘ + Enter to send it.

Two things to check along the way. Google's page does not list the setting as a requirement for compose or formatting, so these keys may work even when the list groups fail. Click inside the message body first, so the keys go to the draft and not to the sidebar.
The usual mistake is pressing Ctrl instead of Command. Nothing happens, and it looks like the setting is broken. Switch to Command and try again before you open any settings page.
Customize Gmail shortcut keys on a Mac
Gmail lets you change some shortcut keys, but custom shortcuts are a separate switch. Go to Settings > Advanced, click Enable next to Custom keyboard shortcuts, then click Save Changes.
Next, go to Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts. Click in the box beside an action, type the new key, and save. Each key can refer to only one action, so choose a key that nothing else uses in Gmail.
Check macOS for shortcut conflicts

Sometimes macOS grabs a key combination before Gmail sees it. Apple's current steps are: choose the Apple menu, open System Settings, select Keyboard, then click Keyboard Shortcuts. Pick a category and look for the shortcut with the warning icon.

Double-click that shortcut and press the new combination. Apple's older page for macOS 10.15 Catalina uses System Preferences > Keyboard > Shortcuts and a yellow warning badge. The names changed, but the idea is the same. Find the conflict, then move it.
What to try when shortcuts still do nothing

Work through these checks in order. Start with focus. Press Esc once or twice, then click the message list. That returns keyboard focus to Gmail. Press E on a selected email to test. The Inbox Zero guide uses this check, and E acts on the message you selected, so pick one you can move.

If the keys still fail, look at extensions. In Chrome, open chrome://extensions/shortcuts and change or remove any shortcut that overlaps with Gmail. In Edge, use edge://extensions/shortcuts. Last, clear Gmail's site data. In Chrome, open chrome://settings/content/all, search for mail.google.com, and choose Clear data. Expect to sign in again afterward.
Non-US keyboards and layouts

Some keys fail on non-US layouts. A troubleshooting guide notes that the # key and similar keys can break. You have two fixes. Switch to a US layout while you use Gmail, or turn on custom shortcuts and remap the actions that fail.
Switch layouts in your Mac's keyboard settings, not inside Gmail. Test each key after you switch, because one fix may work for one key and not another.
Multiple Gmail accounts

Shortcuts are set per account. If you sign in to a work account and a personal account, turn the setting on in each one. Test them separately. The setting you chose in one account does not carry over to the other.
Common mistakes to avoid

items: Turning the setting on in one account, then testing in another.
Typing ? inside a message, which adds a question mark to your draft.
Pressing Ctrl on a Mac. Gmail's Mac keys use Command.
Closing Settings without clicking Save Changes.
Expecting the b Snooze shortcut in classic Gmail. Google says it is not available there.
Blaming Gmail when a macOS shortcut already owns the key combination.

blocks.text: Where to go next

Once shortcuts work, the next time-saver is a signature, so you stop retyping your sign-off. [Create an email signature in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/create-an-email-signature-in-gmail) shows the steps. If you want mail to wait, [schedule an email to send later](/how-to/schedule-an-email-to-send-later-in-gmail). For mail you regret sending too early, [undo send in Gmail](/how-to/undo-send-in-gmail) shows the browser steps. To sort incoming mail automatically, [create a filter in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/create-a-filter-in-gmail).
What this guide could not check

Google's help page says Settings tab, while the Inbox Zero guide says General tab. Gmail also needs a signed-in account, so these steps were not checked on a live Gmail screen. If a label looks different, follow the Keyboard shortcuts section by name, not the tab name.

faq.question: Is there an official Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: No official native Gmail app for Mac appears in the sources behind this guide, so these steps use Gmail in a browser. Some third-party guides suggest installing Gmail from Chrome as an app. Google's pages did not confirm that route.

faq.question: Why does the ? key do nothing in Gmail?
faq.answer: Shortcuts may still be off, or your cursor may be in a text box. Confirm that Keyboard shortcuts on is selected, click the message list, and press ? again. If it still fails, check extensions and clear mail.google.com site data.

faq.question: Do Gmail shortcuts work in Safari on a Mac?
faq.answer: A troubleshooting guide says Gmail works in Safari, Chrome, Firefox, and Edge when cookies and JavaScript are on. Reports specific to Safari were not verified, so test the ? key first.

faq.question: Do I press Command or Control on a Mac?
faq.answer: Press Command (⌘) for Gmail's Mac shortcuts. Google's tables say Ctrl because they list PC keys. Next misspelled word, ⌘ + ;, is listed as Mac only.

faq.question: Can I change Gmail's shortcut keys?
faq.answer: Yes. Turn on Custom keyboard shortcuts under Settings > Advanced, click Save Changes, then change keys under Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts. One key can refer to only one action.

faq.question: Does turning on Gmail shortcuts change anything on my Mac?
faq.answer: No. It is a Gmail setting that lives in your browser. Apple's Keyboard settings stay as they were. If a macOS shortcut conflicts with a Gmail key, change the macOS shortcut in System Settings.

faq.question: Why is the Snooze shortcut missing in Gmail?
faq.answer: Google says the Snooze shortcut, b, is not available in classic Gmail. This guide did not confirm which Gmail layout you see, so open the ? dialog and check the list it shows you.

faq.question: Do all Gmail shortcuts need the setting turned on?
faq.answer: Not all of them. Google notes that action, jumping, thread selection, navigation, and application shortcuts depend on the setting. Compose and formatting shortcuts carry no such note, so test them if they fail.

task: Turn on Gmail keyboard shortcuts on a Mac
appliesTo: Gmail in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge on macOS
requirements: A Mac with Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge
A Gmail account you can sign in to
Cookies and JavaScript turned on in the browser
Gmail open in one browser tab, not a mail app

steps.name: Open Gmail in your browser
steps.text: Open Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge and go to mail.google.com. Sign in to the Google account you want to change. Gmail needs cookies and JavaScript turned on to run.
steps.tip: Signed-out visits redirect to Google sign-in, so you cannot reach the settings page until you log in.

steps.name: Click the Settings gear icon
steps.text: Look at the top right corner of the Gmail window. Click the gear icon labeled Settings.

steps.name: Choose See all settings
steps.text: Choose See all settings from the menu that appears. This opens the full settings page.

steps.name: Open the Settings tab
steps.text: Click the Settings tab on the full settings page. Google's help page names it this way. Some guides call the first tab General, so look for the section rather than the tab name.
steps.tip: Tab names can differ, so the section name matters more than the tab name.

steps.name: Scroll to Keyboard shortcuts
steps.text: Scroll down the Settings tab until you reach the section titled Keyboard shortcuts.

steps.name: Select Keyboard shortcuts on
steps.text: Select the option labeled Keyboard shortcuts on. This is the switch that enables Gmail's shortcuts.

steps.name: Save your changes
steps.text: Scroll to the bottom of the settings page and click Save Changes. The setting does not stick until you save it.

steps.name: Confirm with the question mark
steps.text: Make sure Gmail is the active window and your cursor is not in a text box. Press ? (Shift + /). The Keyboard shortcuts dialog should open.
steps.tip: If the dialog does not open, check that the cursor is not inside a message or search box.

steps.name: Enable from the dialog if needed
steps.text: If the dialog shows an Enable or Disable link, press Tab once to reach it. If the link says Enable, press Enter. Then press ? again to confirm.

steps.name: Test on a selected email
steps.text: Click one email in your inbox to select it, then press E. The Inbox Zero guide uses E as its test. Pick a message you do not mind moving, because E acts on the selected email.
steps.tip: Choose a low-stakes message for this test, since the key acts on whatever is selected.

shortcuts.action: Jump to next misspelled word (Mac only)
Return focus to the message list

troubleshooting.problem: Shortcuts do nothing after you save
troubleshooting.fix: Press Esc once or twice, then click the message list. This returns keyboard focus to Gmail. Then test again with E on a selected email.

troubleshooting.problem: A browser extension uses the same key
troubleshooting.fix: In Chrome, open chrome://extensions/shortcuts and change or remove overlapping shortcuts. In Edge, use edge://extensions/shortcuts.
In Chrome, open chrome://settings/content/all, search for mail.google.com, and choose Clear data. Then sign in again.

troubleshooting.problem: macOS takes the shortcut before Gmail does
troubleshooting.fix: Open System Settings, choose Keyboard, then Keyboard Shortcuts. Double-click the shortcut with the warning icon and press a new combination.

troubleshooting.problem: A key fails on your keyboard layout
troubleshooting.fix: Switch to a US layout while using Gmail, or turn on Custom keyboard shortcuts and remap the failing actions.

troubleshooting.problem: Only one of your accounts responds
troubleshooting.fix: Shortcuts are set per account. Turn them on in each account, then test each one separately.
